speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you are having nightmares during your sleep, or do you wake up screaming without remembering a dream?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall having a vivid, scary dream right before you wake up, and do these episodes typically happen in the second half of the night? I also need to know if you have had any recent stressful events or changes in your routine that might be causing anxiety.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you recall the scary dreams, these are likely nightmares rather than sleep terrors, but I need to rule out underlying medical causes. Do you snore loudly, gasp for air, or have pauses in your breathing while you sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience daytime sleepiness, hyperactivity, or difficulty concentrating at school? I also need to know if there is a family history of sleep apnea or obesity.

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings in other systems. No history of trauma or significant stress identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recollection of dreams and lack of physical signs, this appears to be primary nightmares rather than sleep terrors or apnea. I will request a sleep study to definitively rule out any underlying sleep-disordered breathing. REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Not indicated at this stage based on history and normal physical examination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the sleep study is not indicated and there are no signs of sleep apnea or other medical issues, I will focus on behavioral factors. Can you describe your bedtime routine and any specific worries you have before going to sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings in other systems. No history of trauma or significant stress identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have mentioned bedtime procrastination, so what specific activities or thoughts keep you from wanting to go to bed? Are there any particular fears or worries that come up right before you try to sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings in other systems. No history of trauma or significant stress identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the absence of trauma, stress, or physiological markers, this presentation is consistent with a primary sleep disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmares Disorder
